tasks.title: 3-tier agency schema + atomic provisioning
tasks.notes: REMAINING: agency authz policy, AgencyRole runtime validation, denormalized agencyId + cross-agency invariant on agent-owned models, agency-isolation tests.

prep.what: Finish the 3-tier agency auth system: add agency authz policy, AgencyRole runtime validation, denormalize agencyId onto every agent-owned model, and prove cross-agency isolation with tests.
prep.understand: The atomic provisioning (`provisionAgencyOfOne`) and ALS-scoped `db` guard are already solid. An Agency owns many Tenants; every agent-facing model must carry a denormalized `agencyId` alongside `tenantId` with a `child.agencyId == parent.agencyId` cross-check. `dbAdmin` is the ONLY cross-agency hatch — that invariant must hold in tests.
approach: Add `AgencyRole` enum + validate it at the policy boundary (fail-closed on unknown roles)
Write the agency authz policy: role → permitted actions matrix, wired into the existing ALS-scoped `db` guard
Migration: add `agencyId` to all agent-facing models and a DB constraint asserting `child.agencyId == parent.agencyId`
Agency-isolation test suite: assert tenant A's agent cannot read tenant B's data even within the same agency, and cross-agency access is impossible
resources: ALS context setup in existing auth middleware
`test:tenants` — existing tenant isolation test patterns to extend

tasks.title: pending_outbound approval state machine + DB guard
tasks.notes: Foundation done (PendingOutbound model, DB CHECKs, queueForApproval, assertDispatchable, 7 tests green). REMAINING: approve/decline/expire transitions, authenticated one-time token consumption, claim→deliver→mark-sent worker.

prep.what: Wire the 3 missing state transitions on `PendingOutbound` — approve, decline, expire — plus the authenticated one-time token consumption and the Inngest worker that claims and sends.
prep.understand: Human approval isn't just UX — it's the LGPD legitimate-interest control point. The token must be consumed exactly once (atomic `consumedAt`), and every external send must go through `assertDispatchable` first. The DB CHECK constraints already enforce the status invariants at the database level.
approach: Implement `approve`: verify `approvalTokenHash`, check not expired and not consumed, set `approvedAt` + `approvedByUserId` + `consumedAt` atomically in one `UPDATE WHERE consumedAt IS NULL`
Implement `decline` and `expire` transitions (status changes + optional reason field)
Build the claim→deliver→mark-sent Inngest worker: claim by setting `status='claimed'`, call `assertDispatchable`, send via `ChannelRouter`, mark `sent`
Tests: token replay (second use must fail 409/400), expiry edge case, two workers racing to claim the same token
resources: Inngest `onUserCreated` function — pattern for worker structure
ALS-scoped `queueForApproval` — the entrypoint that mints the token

tasks.title: Observability: Sentry + Inngest dashboard lockdown + payload scrub
tasks.notes: Sentry error monitoring with token+PII scrubbing; lock the Inngest dashboard + scrub secrets from job payloads.

prep.what: Wire Sentry error monitoring with PII scrubbing and lock down the Inngest dashboard so agent job payloads can't leak.
prep.understand: Two security surfaces in 30 minutes: Sentry must never log brandbook content, message text, or auth tokens from the agent layer. Inngest's dashboard endpoint, if open, would expose job payloads. Both are mechanical config tasks with no architecture decisions.
approach: Install `@sentry/nextjs`, init in `sentry.server.config.ts` with a `beforeSend` hook that strips fields matching `/token|secret|key|content|brandbook|message|recipient/i`
Set `INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY` env var to lock the `/api/inngest` endpoint, verify the dashboard is protected
Add a scrub utility that redacts sensitive keys from Inngest job event data before any Sentry capture fires inside workers
resources: Inngest docs: `INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY` env var + dashboard access control
`app/api/inngest/route.ts` — where to verify signing key middleware
P&S §3.5 — payload scrub spec and field list

tasks.title: Route takeoff measurements to trades at the seam
tasks.notes: Every measurement collapses to one anonymous kind=custom $0 line today. Switch on kind: area→flooring, derived wall SF→painting, line(LF)→wall-linear/trim, count(EA)→doors/tile. Tag each line with a trade via the core-vs-subbed helper.

prep.what: Update `TakeoffEstimateSeeder` to route each measurement type to the correct trade line instead of collapsing everything into one generic `$0` custom line.
prep.understand: The Takeoff API returns measurements with a `kind` field (area/line/count). Today the seeder drops that and emits one anonymous line. Rafa wants: area SF → flooring, LF → trim/wall-linear, count → door/tile. Use `ProjectType::isCoreTrade()` to set `crew_type` (painting/flooring=own_team, rest=subcontracted). This is the foundation for priced lines in t48.
approach: Open `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php` — find the loop where measurements are emitted as estimate lines
Add a `routeToTrade(string $kind): array` helper returning `['trade' => ..., 'crew_type' => ...]` based on measurement kind (area→flooring, line→trim, count→doors)
For each measurement, emit a `LineItemFactory` line with the trade tag and the correct `crew_type` from `ProjectType::isCoreTrade()`
Regression test: seed a fixture takeoff, assert area measurements become flooring lines, LF become trim lines, counts become door lines — each with the correct crew_type

tasks.title: Derive wall PAINT area (perimeter × height) — the missing painting measurement
tasks.notes: A 2D plan has no wall height so painting gets ZERO auto-sqft today. Add wall_height_ft (estimate default + per-room override), preserve geometry.rings/meta.perimeter from takeoff API, emit Wall paint area line per room.

prep.what: Add wall height input to estimates and compute wall paint sqft (perimeter × height) per room from the takeoff geometry — so painting jobs get real square footage instead of zero.
prep.understand: 2D blueprints have no Z-axis, so wall area must be computed as `perimeter × wall_height_ft`. The seeder currently drops `geometry.rings` / `meta.perimeter` from the API response. You need: the height field on estimates (default 9 ft), perimeter from API preserved in seeder, and a 'Wall paint area' line per room.
approach: Migration: add `wall_height_ft DECIMAL(5,2) DEFAULT 9.0 NULLABLE` to `estimates` table
Add wall height input to `Estimates/Edit.vue` (number field near estimate metadata); also expose it on `Takeoff/Index.vue`
In `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php::seedFromTakeoff`, stop dropping geometry — read `room.meta.perimeter` (or sum from `room.geometry.rings` if absent)
For each room with a perimeter, compute `wall_area_sqft = perimeter × estimate->wall_height_ft` and emit as a painting area line via `LineItemFactory`
resources: `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php` — where geometry is currently dropped (search for `perimeter` or `rings`)
